lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: two-rule numerical patterns

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: Pattern A is 3, 7, 11, 15. Pattern B is 6, 14, 22, 30. How are corresponding terms related?

steps: Each Pattern B term is twice its Pattern A partner.
The relationship continues because Pattern B also grows by twice as much each step.
workedSolution.answer: Each term in Pattern B is 2 times the corresponding term in Pattern A.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Pattern A starts at 14 and adds 7. Pattern B starts at 10 and adds 12. Using Pattern A as x and Pattern B as y, which point represents term 4?
1128 counters are split into 24 equal groups. Which pair of equations represents the model?
A rectangle has area 396 square units and one side length is 12 units. What is the missing side length?

Use these partial-quotients steps to solve 6785 ÷ 81:
6785 - 81 × 80 = 305
305 - 81 × 3 = 62
What is the quotient and remainder?
